To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the prognostic value in breast cancer of the plasmino-gen activation system is not only determined by the levels of the individual components, but is also dependent on the balance between these components, i.e. the ratio between tPA:PA1-1 complex, free uncomplexed tP A and free, un-complexed PAI-1.
elevated levels of (free) tPA in the pellet extracts are related to improved RFS and OS, and that elevated levels of the tPa:PAI- 1 complex in the cytosols are associated with a poor prognosis.
the levels of the tPa:PaI-1 complex in breast cancer cytosols, and the levels of total tPA and PAi-1 in breast cancer pellets, are prognostic markers for survival of breast cancer patient.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the prognostic value and the clinical relevance of tPA and its complex with PAI-1 in breast cancer.
a novel prognostic marker for breast cancer, namely the tPA: PAI-1 complex.
the prognostic value and clinical relevance of components of the fibrinolytic system in breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
both tPA and tPA:PA1-1 complex in cytosols as well as tPA in the detergent-insoluble fraction of breast tumours are independent predictors of poor prognosis.
the prognostic value provided by the determination of the tPA and/or tPA:PA-1 complex in cytosols is comparable to that of PAI-1 in cytosols.

both cytosolic and pellet extracts provide prognostic information on tPA and tPA:PA1-1 complex, but the cytosolic extracts provide prognostically relevant information on the tPA: PAI-1 complex, and the pellet extracts on tPA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the prognostic value is dependent on the assay method, and that it is important to use the same method in the analysis of the different forms of the plasmino-gen activation system.
the complex of tissue-type plasmogen activator (TPA) and the type-1 plasminogen inhibitor (PAI) is an independent prognostic factor for breast cancer patients.

the levels of tPA, the tPA: PAI-1 complex as well as free, uncomplex PAI-1 in the cytosolic extracts were all related to the prognosis of breast cancer patients, whereas only the levels of t PA in the detergent extracts of the 100 000g pellet extracts were associated with a prolonged survival.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the determination of the tPA/PAI-1 ratio is of prognostic significance in breast cancer patients, and this information is independent from the levels of tPA or PAI-1 alone.
it is the free, unbound forms of tPA and/or of PAI-1 that provide the prognostic information, while the tPA: PAI-1 complex does not.

the prognostic value provided by tPA and the PAI-1:tPA complex is different and depends upon whether the tPA or the PAI- 1:tPA complex levels are measured in cytosolic fractions or in detergent extracts of ultracentrifuged pellets.
